references.text: The continuation of the account shows that the man's son was healed at exactly the moment Jesus said, "Your son lives", confirming the power of Jesus' words ([ref:Joh 4:51-53|John 4:51-53]).

Context for the healing: The royal official came to Jesus and asked him to come down and heal his son, but Jesus healed with just a word without being physically present ([ref:Joh 4:46-49|John 4:46-49]).

Jesus encourages faith in his words before the miracle occurs, just as this official believed Jesus' words and went on his way: "Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see God's glory?" ([ref:Joh 11:40|John 11:40]).
A parallel to healing at a distance through faith: The officer in Capernaum believed that Jesus could heal with just a word, and Jesus commended his faith ([ref:Matt 8:8-13|Matthew 8:8-13]).
Also in Luke's account of the officer's servant, Jesus heals at a distance, and the sick person is healed without Jesus being physically present ([ref:Luk 7:2-10|Luke 7:2-10]).
The Canaanite woman showed great faith, and her daughter was healed the moment Jesus spoke his word – a parallel to healing through faith in Jesus' words alone ([ref:Matt 15:28|Matthew 15:28]).

The official demonstrated the nature of faith by believing Jesus' words and acting on them without visible proof: "Faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see" ([ref:Hebr 11:1|Hebrews 11:1]).
Another example in the Gospel of John where people believed Jesus' words: The disciples believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken ([ref:Joh 2:22|John 2:22]).
Jesus blesses those who believe without seeing, as this official is an example – he believed Jesus' words and went home without having seen any healing yet ([ref:Joh 20:29|John 20:29]).

God's healing word in the Old Testament: "He sent his word and healed them" – Jesus' healing word to the official reflects God's sovereign power to heal through his word ([ref:Sal 107:20|Psalm 107:20]).
